sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Public Commercial Web Scraping and Proxy API Gateways

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations), Articles 4-14 and 18-22; Reglamentada por Decreto Ejecutivo No. 17 de 16 de mayo de 1997; applicable registration rules of the Registro Publico de Panama.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Publico de Panama - Seccion de Fundaciones de Interes Privado (Public Registry of Panama, Private Interest Foundations Section)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Publica Constitutiva (Acta Fundacional) together with the Reglamento (Foundation Bylaws), presented as the foundation charter
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Law 25 of 1995 (Art. 12) requires the foundation to hold an initial patrimony adequate for its stated purposes; established market and registry practice requires a minimum endowment of US$10,000.00, contributed in cash or in kind and declared in the charter. No escrow account is statutorily mandated; the endowment is evidenced by a bank certificate or asset inventory and the foundation is not subject to paid-up capital filing obligations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Foundation Charter and Bylaws dated ____ are ratified and adopted; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the initial endowment of Ten Thousand United States Dollars (US$10,000.00) is irrevocably subscribed to the Foundation patrimony per Law 25 of 1995; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office is established at ____, Panama City, Panama, with ____ as Resident Agent; FURTHER RESOLVED, that ____, ____, and ____ are appointed to the Foundation Council until resignation or removal; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Council Chair is authorized to execute all registry filings and obtain municipal, environmental, and operational licenses for the web data and API services business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Publico de Panama - Departamento de Nombres, via the e-RPP / PANATRAM online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three proposed foundation names (with 'Fundacion' suffix) to the Public Registry for clearance against existing corporations and foundations. The name must be distinguishable from registered entities and not contravene public order. Upon approval, the registry issues a name reservation certificate valid for a fixed non-renewable period, which must be attached to the notarial deed.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form (Solicitud de Reserva de Nombre)
Copy of founder's passport or corporate identity documents
Notarized power of attorney appointing the Panamanian resident agent (if filing through counsel)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity, file an immediate alternate name request; no appeal is required as refiling is instantaneous. Conflicting identical names are resolved by priority of registration; the below-listed dossiers are resubmitted with the new name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Foundation Charter and Bylaws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaria Publica del Circuito de Panama (Panamanian Civil-Law Notary selected by the Founder)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founder executes the Escritura Publica Constitutiva (Acta Fundacional) before the notary. The deed must contain: the foundation name, the initial endowment declaration, a detailed purpose clause covering ISIC 6201 activities (commercial web scraping, data pipeline and proxy API gateway services), the registered office address in Panama, the resident agent appointment, the members of the Foundation Council, the beneficiaries, and any optional Protector. The Reglamento (bylaws) sets internal governance, quorum, and amendment rules. Both Spanish and English versions are signed; the Spanish text prevails.
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate issued by the Registro Publico
Draft Charter and Reglamento in Spanish (original)
Evidence of initial endowment (bank certificate or notarized asset inventory)
Passport copies of the founder, all Foundation Council members, and any Protector
Letter of acceptance from the Panamanian resident agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary detects legal inconsistencies in the draft, the parties amend the draft prior to execution at no prejudice. A defective executed deed may be cured by a rectification deed (escritura aclaratoria) executed before the same notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Publico de Panama - Seccion de Fundaciones de Interes Privado (e-RPP filing accepted)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the authentic first copy (copia autentica) of the notarial deed with the Public Registry together with the official registration fee of approximately US$250.00. The Registry examines the charter for legality, issues a registration certificate (ficha registral), and records the foundation in the Registro de Fundaciones. The Private Interest Foundation acquires separate legal personality only upon this registration.
required_dossiers: Authentic first copy of the Escritura Publica Constitutiva
Certified copy of the Reglamento (bylaws), if contained in a separate instrument
Official payment receipt for the B/.250.00 registration fee
Identification statements of the Foundation Council members and Protector (as requested by the Registry)
Completed Registro application questionnaire
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues prevenciones (observations), cure the deficiencies in writing within 10 working days by filing corrected schedules or a rectification deed. If registration is refused, file for reconsideration with the Director of the Registry or pursue an 'amparo de garantias' proceeding before the civil courts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldia de Panama - Ventanilla Unica de Avisos de Operacion (SETAM online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the Municipality of Panama for the Aviso de Operacion and municipal patent covering technology and data-service activities. Submit the registered foundation charter, lease or title for the Panama office, RUC certificate, and identification of the Foundation Council members. The Municipality performs an administrative inspection of the premises, and upon approval the foundation receives the municipal operating license and is enrolled in the municipal tax roll.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the registered foundation charter
Preliminary taxpayer registration (RUC) certificate from the Direccion General de Ingresos
Lease agreement or property title for the registered office in Panama
Passport copies of the Foundation Council members
Municipal tax clearance (paz y salvo) for the premises, if previously occupied
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or rejected, correct the file on the SETAM portal and resubmit within 30 days of the initial resolution to avoid late fees; schedule a re-inspection of the premises. An administrative appeal lies with the Municipal Treasury if the denial persists.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Fire Safety, Occupational Health, and Environmental Compliance Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SINAPROC (Sistema Nacional de Proteccion Civil), MINSA (Ministerio de Salud), and MiAMBIENTE (Ministerio de Ambiente)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the Certificado de Prevencion de Incendios from SINAPROC following a fire-safety inspection of the office (extinguishers, smoke detectors, evacuation signage). Submit the MINSA environmental health registration for office workplaces. File the MiAMBIENTE Category 1 environmental registration if minor building conversion works occur. Retain e-waste disposal agreements with MiAMBIENTE-authorized handlers for decommissioned servers and IT equipment.
required_dossiers: SINAPROC fire-prevention inspection application, building floor plan, and lease
MINSA environmental-health form for office workplaces
MiAMBIENTE Category 1 Registration form (Registro de Impacto Ambiental), if triggered
E-waste handling agreement with an authorized recycler
CSS (Caja de Seguro Social) employer registration certificate, if hiring personnel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SINAPROC or MINSA inspection flags deficiencies, implement corrective measures within the authority's stated timeline and request re-inspection at no additional statutory cost. Administrative reconsideration (recurso de reconsideracion) is available before the issuing authority, followed by appeal to the respective Ministry.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipio de Panama - Direccion de Avisos de Operacion, coordinated with the Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) through the Single Window for Investment (Ventanilla Unica para la Inversion)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operacion y Patente Municipal (Municipal Operating Notice and Business Patent) for data technology and API gateway services

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) - Direccion de Verificacion del Desempeno Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 1 - EIA Registration only (Registro de Impacto Ambiental) under Decreto Ejecutivo No. 123 de 14 de agosto de 2009; office-based software, web scraping, and API data services are low-impact activities and do not require a full EIA study
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial effluents or point-source discharges; domestic wastewater must comply with MINSA sanitary sewer discharge norms; zero VOC, particulate, or combustion emissions since no manufacturing process is operated; cooling and electronic equipment must be maintained to prevent refrigerant leakage per national ozone-depleting substance rules; e-waste (servers, network hardware) must be transferred to MiAMBIENTE-authorized e-waste handlers pursuant to Resolucion No. 590-2012; noise levels in the office district must remain within municipal ordinance limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Certificado de Prevencion de Incendios from SINAPROC (fire extinguishers, smoke detection, illuminated egress signs, evacuation plan, and quarterly fire-drill log); workplace environmental-health clearance from MINSA for the office; structural and electrical-load certification for IT racks issued by the Municipality's engineering section; occupational-hazard employer registration with the Caja de Seguro Social and compliance with Panamanian workplace safety regulations for monitor-display workstations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); e-Tax portal: https://etax.mef.gob.pa; official website: https://dgi.mef.gob.pa
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Engage a licensed Panamanian resident agent (agente residente) for the PIF. 2) Execute the foundation deed (acta fundacional) and reglamento and record with the Registro Público de Panamá. 3) File via the DGI e-Tax portal the RUC application (Solicitud de Registro Único de Contribuyente) attaching the certified foundation deed, resident agent acceptance, identity documents of council members, and proof of registered address. 4) Obtain the RUC certificate and activate the e-Tax digital credentials (clave de acceso). 5) Register for ITBM as a collector when habitual taxable services are intended and enroll in the electronic invoicing system (SFE). 6) Obtain the municipal Aviso de Operación/business license for the registered commercial activity. A foreign entity may act through its local fiscal representative; the PIF functions as the operative taxpayer and foreign founders/beneficiaries need no personal Panamanian TIN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or pass-through election exists; a PIF is the entity-level taxpayer for Panama-source income (general corporate ISR 25%), and all foreign-source income is expressly exempt under Panama's territorial system. Available elections and mechanisms: (i) small-taxpayer ITBM simplified regime election for annual gross income at or below USD 36,000; (ii) charter-level elections under Ley 25 de 1995 on distributions to beneficiaries and reincorporation of surplus; (iii) election of the DGI transfer-pricing documentation safe harbors under Ley 254 de 2019 for related-party cross-border service contracts; (iv) application of the Multinational Company Headquarters (SEM Law, Ley 41 de 2007) incentive regime if administrative/back-office functions are established. Panama does not provide domestic hybrid-mismatch or check-the-box elections; hybrid mismatch outcomes are managed under BEPS Action 2-compliant disclosure in the annual sworn returns.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBM – Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (Panamanian VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general de minimis threshold: any person habitually transferring taxable goods or rendering taxable services in Panama must register as an ITBM collector. A small-taxpayer option (quarterly settlement at reduced rate) is available for gross income up to USD 36,000 per annum.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing under the DGI 'Sistema de Facturación Electrónica (SFE)' with phased rollout based on annual gross income and taxpayer category. Invoices must be issued in XML/PDF-A through certified software and transmitted to DGI at issuance; each invoice carries a DGI-authorized numeration range and a verifiable QR code. The model is advance authorization with immediate transmission (not full real-time central clearance). Digital signature (Firma Electrónica Avanzada) is mandatory for issuance; input ITBM credits are denied for non-compliant paper or unauthorized invoices. API integration with the e-Tax platform is supported for ERP/automated data-pipeline billing.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Panama are zero-rated at 0% upon physical exit supported by the customs export declaration. Services qualify for 0% ITBM when provided to a non-resident recipient and economically utilized entirely abroad, including data processing, software development, and commercial web-scraping/API gateway services, provided the recipient is non-resident, the service is not consumed or personally used in Panama, and consideration is paid from abroad. The PIF must maintain stream-of-activities evidence showing the scraping targets, proxy/delivery infrastructure, and server-side data flows remain outside Panamanian territory to sustain the offshore characterization.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación / FUE) for physical goods
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill or electronic transport evidence
Commercial invoice and service contract (identifying non-resident recipient and offshore use)
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT or banking credit evidence of foreign payment
Certificate of service utilization abroad (testimonio de utilización en el exterior)
ITBM zero-rating register reconciliation filed in the periodic ITBM return
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Panama imposes no exchange-control repatriation statute, but proceeds must be credited to Panama within 180 days as documentary proof of foreign-source/export status; failure to repatriate or evidence payment triggers recharacterization as Panama-source income and loss of the zero-rating. DGI audit scrutiny focuses on fictitious exports, back-to-back invoicing, and shell foreign recipients. Fraudulent zero-rating claims result in retroactive assessment of the full 7% ITBM from the date of supply, statutory surcharges and late-interest (reconocimiento) under the Código Fiscal, fines (including up to 200% of the omitted tax for reiterated infractions), and criminal defraudación fiscal prosecution where falsified export documentation or fictitious counterparties are proven. The applicable assessment limitation period is the general statute of limitations under Panamanian tax law, extendable in cases of omission or fraudulent conduct.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) — no standalone central bank exists; Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as fiscal agent and clearinghouse operator for the U.S.-dollarized financial system.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama uses the U.S. dollar as sole legal tender and maintains no exchange-control law. Current and capital account transactions are fully convertible without central bank approval; profit remittances and capital repatriation are unrestricted, subject only to AML/CFT record-keeping and reporting obligations under Law 23 of 2015 and SBP Agreement 002-2018.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no statutory surrender timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or central bank reporting requirement for export proceeds. U.S. dollar receipts are freely retainable, transferable, and settleable in any clearing channel.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium. Panama has no distinct electronic-money institution (EMI) licensing regime; payment service providers require a banking license or SBP fintech sandbox authorization. Offshore digital EMIs such as Revolut or Wise are not domestic clearing participants and cannot act as the PIF's primary treasury rail; they may be used only as ancillary collection channels through a licensed local partner bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Panama law does not mandate physical appearance of directors for account opening, but tier-1 banks commonly require at least one foundation council member or authorized representative to attend an in-person or video-verified interview under enhanced due diligence. Remote onboarding may proceed with notarized and apostilled corporate documents, the original foundation charter, a registered foundation resolution, and completed beneficial-ownership forms; fully anonymous foundations cannot open bank accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undisclosed beneficial ownership or nominee council members
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled private interest foundation charter, certificate of registration from the Public Registry, foundation council resolution, sworn beneficial-ownership declaration, passport copies, and utility-style proof of residential address for each council member and beneficiary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk commerce scraping and API data gateway operations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed commercial business plan, customer or counterparty list, data acquisition legality opinion under Panama and target-market laws, privacy policy, SOC 2 / ISO 27001 report, and contractual evidence of legitimate API usage and data-source authorization.

AML/CFT digital-asset policy, blockchain transaction analytics reports, verified exchange KYC/transaction records, source-of-wealth statement, and a treasury segregation schedule proving only regulated banking channels receive settlement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large unexplained initial capital injection or fast-structuring of the foundation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed source-of-funds declaration, independent bank reference letters, audited financial statements or interim management accounts of the settlor/shareholder, transaction forecast, and evidence of corporate substance such as a physical registered agent with KYC responsibilities.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route shareholder or settlor capital via SWIFT MT103 (or Fedwire/CHIPS where the remitter is in the United States) into the PIF's Panama operational or escrow account. Reference the PIF legal name and 'Capital Contribution to Private Interest Foundation' in the SWIFT Field 70 remittance line; no central bank authorization is required. For commercial service receivables, the invoice description should state 'Public Data Pipeline / API Gateway Services' to match the beneficial owner's declared business scope. Bank records must be retained for at least five years under Panama's AML/CFT framework.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Disburse vendor and infrastructure payments using SWIFT MT103 messages over correspondent USD clearing (CHIPS/Fedwire) for cross-border beneficiaries. For large infrastructure settlements, use a commercial letter of credit coupled with bill discounting or documentary collection. Domestic beneficiary payments may be settled through ACH Panamá or RTGS with Banco Nacional de Panamá. Every payment order must be supported by a service agreement and invoice trail to satisfy the bank's enhanced due-diligence review for the ISIC 6201 / data-services sector.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC plain-vanilla foreign exchange forwards denominated in U.S. dollars against EUR/GBP/CHF payables, executed with licensed OECD banks
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for long-term USD funding and non-USD vendor contracts
Offshore nondeliverable forwards (NDFs) for exotic-market currencies, settled in U.S. dollars through SBP-compliant counterparties
Exchange-traded currency futures and vanilla FX options for transactional hedging

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Government Fee (derecho de franquicia anual) for the Private Interest Foundation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Tesoro Nacional / Banco Nacional de Panamá via the licensed resident registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 May; payment window runs from 1 January to 31 May for the current calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late surcharge of B/.50 per month until paid; after three consecutive years of non-payment, the foundation is exposed to administrative strike-off and to registered-agent resignation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Registry update (Registro de Beneficiario Final) declaration of founder, foundation councillors and beneficiaries
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI – Dirección General de Ingresos, Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 May each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of B/.2,000 to B/.10,000 for failure to disclose or for false declarations; repeated non-filing may lead to suspension of the foundation's registration and loss of legal activeness.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax declaration (Declaración Jurada de ISR) if the foundation obtains Panama-source business income from commercial activities such as API data commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 15 March of the year following the close of the preceding calendar tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing interest of 1% per month on unpaid tax, plus fines of B/.50–B/.500 per declaration; unresolved balances may lead to seizure of local assets and registry strike-off after prolonged non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is imposed on a passive Private Interest Foundation. A compulsory independent audit is triggered if Panama-source gross revenues exceed B/.3 million in a tax year, if total assets in Panama exceed B/.3 million, or if the foundation is licensed for financial, trust or fiduciary activities; DGI may also order an audit where accounting irregularities are suspected.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for financial statements used for tax and public-file purposes; non-listed entities may apply Panama GAAP (aligned with US GAAP) with prior approval from the regulators.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 25 of 1995 and AML Decree 2019, a Panama Private Interest Foundation must maintain an updated book of beneficiaries and must notify the registered agent of any change in beneficiary status or foundation council membership within 30 days. The annual DGI beneficial-owner filing confirms that the natural persons controlling or deriving rights from the foundation are current and accurate.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficiaries as required by Law 25 of 1995
Minute Book of the Foundation Council

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $350–$1,200 per annum for a licensed Panama registered agent and registered office
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $4,000–$15,000 for a Panama-scope independent audit; a de minimis PIF with no audit trigger typically pays none

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0% tax on foreign-source income under territorial system; no general tax holiday; 5% SEM regime not applicable absent HQ license. For PIFs engaged in trading/banking inside Panama, an annual real estate/asset tax may apply instead of income tax on certain passive assets.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 140 – Declaración Jurada de Renta (annual income tax return); filed through DGI e-Tax portal (Portal del Contribuyente / e-Tax 2.0).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months of the fiscal year-end; for calendar-year taxpayers, on or before 31 March.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification block: RUC number, entity name, foundation registration number, and fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PIF must have an active RUC. Non-resident foundation council members may act through a resident agent; the PIF should be coded as a 'Fundación de Interés Privado'.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from activities, assets or services located or employed within Panama; includes API services rendered to Panamanian customers and fees for Panama-based server/e-commerce activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report amounts in B/. (PAB). Non-resident PIFs often have no Panama-source receipts; in that case enter 0 and proceed to informative schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income derived from sources outside Panama, such as charges to foreign clients for web scraping/proxy access hosted on foreign infrastructure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclosed for statistical and treaty purposes only; not subject to tax because Panama taxes solely on a territorial basis. Supporting bank statements and geolocation/PID evidence should be retained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable costs, commissions, salaries, depreciation, and interest expenses directly connected with generating taxable Panama-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entity may deduct costs with withholding backing (e.g., expatriate salaries under a non-resident employment contract) only where reciprocal obligations are documented and effectively incurred.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable basis (Panama-source gross receipts minus deductions) multiplied by 25% corporate income tax rate; advances paid in Form 118 are credited against the result.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If all income is foreign-source, enter 0 as taxable tax; the PIF must still file to avoid penalties. Any balance payable is remitted through the e-Tax portal with a Panama bank account or bank payment voucher.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: surcharge of 1% per month or fraction of the tax due, capped at 50% of the final liability; fixed penalty for non-filing/zero filing from B/. 100 to B/. 5,000; monthly interest at the statutory rate (currently approx. 10% p.a. on assessed deficiency). Repeated non-filing may trigger license suspension and the foundation's registry status can be revoked.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 5% withholding on distributions paid out of Panama-taxed profits; 10% withholding on distributions paid out of profits not subject to Panamanian tax (foreign-source/exempt profits).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The PIF must apply the DTA rate by providing to the paying entity or paying itself to the DGI: (i) a Certificate of Tax Residency (TRC) issued by the Panama Director General of Revenue for the relevant year; (ii) a Panama Tax ID / sworn statement confirming beneficial ownership; and (iii) Form 240 (Withholding Tax Return) reporting reduced 5% or 0% rates. Relief is via the DGI's advance-ruling mechanism for withholding at source; otherwise the statutory WHT is withheld and a refund claim must be filed within two years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest paid to non-resident lenders: 0% Panama WHT when the loan is not connected with a Panama permanent establishment (otherwise 6%). Royalties/licence fees paid from Panama for the use of intellectual property (trademarks, patents, software) are subject to 12.5% statutory withholding; DTA rates frequently reduce this to 5%-10%, subject to TRC.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and Master File must be filed when the taxpayer's aggregate annual related-party transactions exceed B/. 250,000 and gross revenue is above B/. 2,000,000; for multinational groups, the Master File is compulsory when consolidated group turnover exceeds B/. 50,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations (ESR, Law 254/2020) apply to PIFs carrying on a relevant activity (distribution and service centre operations; intellectual property holding; financing/leasing; or headquarters). The PIF must show physical premises in Panama, qualified full-time local employees, and actual decision-making in relation to those activities. A PIF holding only passive foreign assets and deriving no Panama-source income is classified as Pure Equity Holding Entity and files a simplified annual substance statement. Failing the substance test invalidates claims of treaty benefits and can trigger de-registration.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting Stripe/USDC payments from Panamanian data-scraping customers and deliberately avoiding the creation of Panama-source invoices, while treating all revenue as foreign-source; or falsely claiming no Panamanian RUC/filing obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment plus interest at the statutory 10% annual rate; administrative surcharge up to 50%; and criminal tax evasion conviction carrying fines equal to 100% of evaded tax and imprisonment of 2 to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation council members and the resident agent who knowingly signed a false declaration are jointly and severally liable for the assessed tax; the court may impose a two-year travel ban, attachment of personal assets, and debarment as a director/trustee.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the PIF as a mere conduit: no office, no staff, no books kept in Panama, no board meetings, while claiming treaty benefits or Panamanian corporate personality to shield beneficial owners from foreign and Panamanian creditors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Sham characterization by the DGI; ESR fines from B/. 10,000 to B/. 1,000,000; cancellation of the foundation registration; and possible revocation of the tax-residency certificate used by your foreign banking relationship.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A court may pierce the veil and order directors to compensate third-party creditors for trades done through the empty shell; directors are also exposed to foreign court judgments and travel restrictions under the Hague Apostille/International Letters Rogatory.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Automated API sales billed in USDC or card rails without verifying end-customer identity or performing KYB/AML screening, particularly when proxy-scraping services are marketed to businesses in sanctioned jurisdictions or to cyber-threat actors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Panama's Law 23 of 2015: administrative fines of up to B/. 5,000,000 for deficient AML/CFT controls; conviction for money laundering may impose from 5 to 12 years' imprisonment and confiscation of all linked digital assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers who 'turned a blind eye' may be prosecuted as principals for laundering, resulting in criminal imprisonment, personal asset freezing, travel bans, and prohibition from future fintech/digital-asset licenses.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing of Related-party API/Data Charges
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Panama PIF charges its foreign software affiliate below-cost fees for API gateway services while the foreign affiliate resells at a premium to end customers, shifting profit from Panama to a zero-tax jurisdiction without a CUP/TNMM analysis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGI can arm's-length adjust the fee, assess underpaid tax plus 1% monthly surcharge and statutory interest, and impose a 20% penalty on the amount of the adjustment if documentation is absent after the 30-day documentary request.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Although TP penalties are generally payable by the entity, directors can be held personally liable for the equivalent of unpaid withholding tax if the mispricing is recharacterized as a constructive distribution; serious fraud referrals can expose them to the criminal penalties in red flag #1.
